You'd think someone wrote the filter that finds the edges of a 7. Nobody did.

A 7 is a bar and a slanted stem, so surely an engineer wrote a filter for horizontal edges and one for diagonals.

Six real handwritten digits, one PIN code. The reader stops on the 7, which becomes a 28 by 28 grid: 784 numbers, 0 for paper, 255 for ink. Nothing else goes in.

A 3 by 3 card of nine weights slides over them: +0.54 +0.69 +0.60 on top, -0.96 -0.68 -0.93 at the bottom. Every stop is 9 pixels times 9 weights, added up: one number. 676 out, blue above zero, amber below. It lights where ink sits above paper: the bottom edge of every stroke. An edge detector.

Three more filters, 2704 numbers. ReLU zeroes the 1570 below zero; max-pool keeps the biggest of every 2 by 2. 676 left, the 7 still visible in every map.

Ten outputs each add up all 676 with their own weights. 7 scores +10.34, the runner-up 3 has +0.93. Softmax: more than 99.99% for 7.

Rewind. At step 0 the nine weights are random, 5.6% of test digits read right, and this 7 reads as a 4. After 1 280 digits: a 7, 71.2%. After 59 968: 94.7%, top row positive, bottom row negative. Each digit nudged the nine numbers toward less error, and an edge detector is what less error looks like.

Nobody wrote the filter. Nine random numbers were nudged by 59 968 handwritten digits until they found edges on their own.

Not shown: the nudge itself (backpropagation) and the other three scans. 6 810 weights, one pass; production readers pass 99%. Every printed number is from the run.

Write a 7 with a bar through the middle. Would this network still call it a 7?

One mechanism at a time. Follow for the next one.

Part 2 of the height sorting build: here's exactly how box size gets determined, line by line.

When a new pallet arrives at the sensor, the first thing the code does is clear the previous result. That matters more than it looks, without it, a short box could inherit a "tall" reading left over from whatever passed through before it.

Then, for the entire time the pallet is passing through the beam, both height sensors are watched continuously and latched the moment either one is broken. This isn't a single check. A box and the pallet carrying it don't reach the sensors at the same instant, so sampling once would risk catching one sensor mid-arrival and missing the other entirely. Latching across the whole pass is what makes the result reliable regardless of timing.

The result, tall or short, gets stored. It isn't used yet, that decision, which direction the box actually gets diverted, is a separate piece of logic entirely, coming in Part 3.

Built and running in FactoryIO, real physics, real classification logic.

When it comes to c-section aftercare, advice is THIN on the ground.

Discharged without even a basic leaflet.

Told to âkeep your wound clean and dryâ.

Warned ânot to lift anything heavier than your babyâ.

But then what? What about the numbness you still have? What about the tugging and tightness? What about YOUR needs? 

You know exercise is important and you want to start moving again, but how do you know whatâs best? What should you look out for?

You know that massaging your scar is a good idea, but how much is too much? What should it feel like? How can you monitor this yourself?

Thatâs where the GOLDILOCKS RULE comes in. 

Too little stretch and load can lead to stiffness through the tissues, reinforcing guarding and protective behaviours. If the scar and surrounding structures arenât able to move freely, you will continue to feel those pinching and tugging sensations when you move.

Too much stretch and load (particularly in early healing) can be inflammatory and cause the body to lay down extra scar tissue, again causing tension. 

The âJUST RIGHTâ amount of stretch and load will gently and progressively improve slide and glide through the âstickyâ tissue layers whilst slowly increasing tolerance to load. This is the sweet spot, and is relevant for both hands on and movement based strategies.

So what does this mean for you in a practical sense?

It means not avoiding movements that are aggravating, but reducing the range to the point at which itâs comfortable. It also means not pushing through pain and ignoring your body. 

It means not avoiding contact with your scar and tummy, but finding techniques that donât cause discomfort. As your tolerance changes, so can your massage choices. It also means not putting up with the pain and doing it anyway - this is NOT helpful. 

I know it can seem like a minefield, but as is often the case, consistency and being kind to yourself wins. 

Remember the GOLDILOCKS RULE:

Not too little.
Not too much. 
Just the right amount.

ðªµ 1501â1532 | The Portuguese in Brazil | Part II

What youâre seeing:
A coast Portugal claimed but did not yet fully control. Portuguese and French merchants came for brazilwood, while trade, captivity and settlement began changing life along the coast.

Why is Brazil named after a tree?
Brazilwood produced a prized red dye. Tupi men cut and carried the logs to ships in exchange for goods including iron axes, knives, shirts and hats.

Why were the French there?
France never signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, which divided newly found lands between Spain and Portugal. Merchants from Normandy and Brittany were already trading for brazilwood by 1505.

Who were the people taken on the Bretoa?
Its 1511 register lists 35 enslaved people, including men, women and young people. One girl is named BrÃ­gida. Their value was taxed for the king.

Was there really a battle?
Yes. Off Pernambuco in February 1531, a French ship fought the Portuguese through the night and following day before surrendering after running out of gunpowder. It was loaded with brazilwood.

What changed at SÃ£o Vicente?
In January 1532, Martim Afonso de Sousa founded a town there. Pero Lopes described towns, laws and marriages, ending with âe ser cada um senhor do seuâ: âand each man master of his own.â

Were the French trying to stay?
Yes. In September 1532, JoÃ£o III reported that a French ship had destroyed a Portuguese trading post at Pernambuco and left 70 men to settle and defend the land. French trade continued, and France later tried to establish a colony at Guanabara Bay in 1555.

Sources: Bretoa (1511); Gonneville (1505); Treaty of Tordesillas (1494); Pero Lopes de Sousa (1530â32); JoÃ£o III (1532); Francis I/Roberval (1541); Jean de LÃ©ry (1578); Gandavo (1576).

To be alive...

Sometimes the hardest part of burnout isn't being exhausted. It's feeling guilty for being exhausted.
You're used to being the person who gets things done.
The one who pushes through.
The one people can depend on.
The one who somehow finds a way, even when you're already running on empty.
So when your brain finally says âI can't,â
it can feel almost impossible to accept.
You know the email only takes a minute.
You know the dishes aren't that difficult.
You know you could do it.
You just can't seem to make yourself care enough to move.
And then comes the guilt.
You rest because you need to.
Then you feel guilty for resting.
So you push yourself again.
And wonder why you're even more exhausted.
Rest isn't something you have to earn by completely breaking down first.
You can be capable and still need a break.
You can be ambitious and still have limits.
Your inability to keep pushing doesn't mean you've lost your ability.
It might just mean you've been pushing for too long.

Hereâs to compassion and grace, the compassion we show one another and the compassion we extend to all living things.

So much unnecessary suffering in the animal kingdom is caused by our waste, our debris, our indifference. We should never forget that our lives are interwoven with the lives of the creatures with whom we share this planet. Their fate and ours are connected.

And yet, even amid so much loss, there are people who care. People working on solutions. And people like this man, who simply saw a living creature in distress and jumped into the water to help.

Never underestimate such small acts of kindness. Compassion for the vulnerable, whether human or animal, reveals something powerful about our humanity.

May we see more of this.
May we be more like this.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
Ever had trouble telling the many-armed creatures of the deep from one another? Dive into this highlight from Enrique Guyotâs exploration for help with your #deepsea animal ID, to keep #brisingid star, #brittlestar, and #crinoid straight.Â  

Along the way, catch glimpses of some of the other local Mariana seafloor residents - a pulsating hydromedusa, sprinting backpack crab, and 26-tentacled burrowing anemone. 
Watch the full video at NautilusLive.org

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: One way animals survive living on the #seafloor over 5,000 meters deep is by eating sediment. Invertebrates like #seapigs, #seacucumbers, and #acornworms will filter nutrients out of the sediment, leaving spiral trails of refuse behind.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While diving on Enrique Guyot, 2,655 meters (8,710 feet) deep, #ROVHercules encountered this slinky, slithery #cuskeel (family Ophidiidae) with an especially long tail. The scientific name comes from the Greek âophisâ meaning âsnake,â although the cusk eel is neither eel nor snake but a fish. In the video, you can clearly see the individualâs lateral line- a collection of sensory organs used to detect vibrations in the water, helping in hunting in the darkness.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
Meet the HARP - a High-frequency Acoustic Recording Package that helps @noaafisheries Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center Cetacean Research Program monitor #whale and #dolphin populations in the #MarianaIslands! 

We kicked off the NA180 expedition retrieving a mooring with nearly 13 months of data onboard and replacing it with a new unit to help build understanding of this special ocean area. This species monitoring helps researchers understand cetacean populations, assess their occurrence and seasonality, and estimate their density in the region.

#oceantech

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
Donât be jelly of this incredible set of observations of #abyssalplain hydrozoans!

While you might be tempted to call all clear, pelagic, drifting predators, âjellyfishâ, did you know this oversimplifies a massive group of cnidarian creatures?Hydromedusae are generally smaller and more delicate than true jellyfish (Scyphomedusae), and feed by trailing stinging tentacles through the water as they drift in the darkness. Watch the full video at NautilusLive.org

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: This fascinating-looking deep-sea creature is a #flatfish- a type of ray-finned fish, flatfish are named after their unique body plan lying on one side and appearing rather flat against the #seafloor. Few vertebrates exhibit this lack of symmetry. This fish was preliminarily identified as a #leopardflounder (Bothus pantherinus) partially because of its âleft-eyedâ body plan, where its right eye migrated through to the other side during the juvenileâs metamorphosis.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: We spotted this pastel #DumboOctopus (genus Grimpoteuthis) while exploring on a never-before-explored seamount approximately 65 km southwest of the coral atoll Ifalik, in Chuuk State, #FederatedStatesofMicronesia. This brief encounter gives us a wonderful look at the #octopusâs unique ear-shaped fins as well as the underside of its eight tentacles- each covered in a single row of suckers and small, strand-like string projections called cirri.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While diving on #RubySeamount- an active submarine #volcano, we witnessed a wealth of #wildlife, including schools of small pink bait fish, a Chaunax #anglerfish, and a #hydromedusa moving through the water column via jet propulsion.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While exploring the waters of the #FederatedStatesofMicronesia with ROVs we spotted this magnificent #Bigfinsquid (genus #Magnapinna) 2,478 meters (8,129 feet) deep. The bigfinâs âsink fishingâ feeding technique involves passively floating with long drawn-out tentacles until one catches prey, which it then retracts towards its mouth for a tasty meal.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: #Chaunacops is a genus of #anglerfish easily recognizable by their round bodies, pink hue, and frowny faces. Also known as #frogfish or coffin fish, they have a fluffy lure that appears as small white dots in the middle of their foreheads.  We spotted this first one on the slopes of Unnamed FSM Seamount 2 (approximately 79 km southwest of Lamotrek Island) at 1,125 meters (3,690 feet deep) .

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While exploring our fourth never-before-seen seamount in the #FederatedStatesofMicronesia, our remotely operated vehicles captured some great footage of the âinflatable Christmas treeâ, a member of the Cladorhizidae family. These #sponges are carnivorous, meaning that, in addition to traditional filter feeding, they use tiny hook-like spicules to nab larger prey.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While exploring the #abyssalplain in the Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas we observed a plethora of the habitatâs squishy and gelatinous #deepsea critters including a beautiful purple #hydromedusa and sparkly, see-through #ctenophore (aka #combjelly).

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
Weâre headed to Wake Island right now to study biology, geology, archaeology, and more of this remote atoll and the deep sea around it. Hereâs why Wake is such an interesting place to learn more about featuring lead scientist Dr. Steve Auscavitch.

#biology #oceanexploration #wakeisland #marinebiology #wwii

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
After a few days of weather, weâre now exploring an abyssal plain in international waters just south of Wake Island. The abyss in this region has not been explored by any other known deep submergence dives.

Weâre expecting to find brown clay with manganese micro-nodules. The primary purpose of this remote operated vehicle (ROV) survey is to collect continuous visual surveys and characterize the organisms that call this extreme environment home. 

Head on over to @nautiluslive to watch the exploration in real time!

ð¸: @mongoose.adventures 

#travel #explore #science

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
Seatbelts everyone, weâre headed on a field trip out to the Pacific Ocean aboard @nautiluslive! Because I think us adults deserve more field trips in our lives, and my favorite thing is being up close with research as it happens.

#ocean #fieldtrip #science #oceanexploration #marinescience

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: During our exploration of the abyssal plain in the far northeastern corner of the US waters in the Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas, our Corps of Exploration witnessed numerous mysterious and beautiful deep-sea critters in class #Hydrozoa. Check out a solitary #hydroid, probably Branchiocerianthus sp., but at least in the family Corymorphidae, and potentially a new family of #Narcomedusae!

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: If youâre looking for a #dumbooctopus, it turns out the abyssal plain in international waters outside the Marshall Islands and Wake Atoll EEZ is the spot to be! Watch as this #octopus shows off its suckered tentacles and ear-shaped fins that earned it the Dumbo name.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While diving on McDonnell Seamount west of #WakeAtoll with ROVs Hercules and Atalanta, our team found this absolutely stunning Iridogorgia magnispiralis coral rising meters high from the seafloor. Thanks to their flexible shape and Hercules-height, #Iridogorgia make particularly great habitat for other #deepseaanimals. Looking down the spiral stalk of this firework coral is truly a wonderful experience.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
Come with me to the Wet Labâbut watch your head! 

After the @nautiluslive remote operated vehicles (ROVs) return from the depths, scientists onboard work quickly to process, document and store the many geological, biological and chemical specimens collected from the seafloor. All of this work happens in the laboratory on the ship and when we get back to shore, the samples are sent out to institutions around the world, including the @mczharvard. 

Thank you @mongoose.adventures for capturing my head-bonk, and for the whole science team for pulling together an incredible expedition to Wake Atoll!

#travel #science #ocean #sea

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: We will never get tired of seeing a Grimpoteuthis #dumbooctopus- especially when the video quality is THIS good! Spotted while exploring an unnamed seamount in the waters near Wake Atoll, 3,730 meters (12,237 feet) deep, we estimate this cephalopod to be almost a meter long. Our #CorpsofExploration was treated to this truly beautiful moment that appears to be almost in slow motion. You can clearly see its large âearâ-shaped fins used to help the animal move in the #deepsea via propulsion.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: While exploring an Unnamed Seamount ~60 nautical miles southeast of #WakeIsland, thousands of meters beneath the surface, we encountered a few unique aquatic friends. #Halosaurs (family Halosauridae) are eel-shaped fish that only live in waters so deep that we only really see them thanks to ROVs like our own Hercules. We spotted this individual at 3,789 meters (12,431 feet) deep.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: During our exploration of the #abyssalplain, 5,800 meters (19,000 feet) deep in international waters northwest of the #MarshallIslands EEZ, we saw this #ctenophore (aka #combjelly) situated right above the seafloor. These fragile, gelatinous marine invertebrates produce shimmering light by moving their comb-like cilia. The team spots its long feeding tentacles draped along the ancient seafloorâs sediment.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
What we bring up from the deep sea to the surface helps us identify new species, better understand life that lives on the seafloor, and learn more about our planet. On board the ocean expedition I just completed on @nautiluslive, I asked some of the science team members to show me what they think are their most interesting samples of the expedition, including some potentially new species to science! 

#ocean #science #nautilus #deepsea #biology

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: During the NA181 expedition exploring the deep sea around #WakeAtoll, we spotted multiple baby #squatlobsters while diving on seamounts with our ROVs! Despite their names, these small, flat marine crustaceans are actually more related to hermit crabs than lobsters. Thanks to our pilots and video engineers, who worked extra hard to get zoomed-in shots of these tiny #crustaceans.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: We witnessed all manner of #deepsea life while exploring the abyssal plain in the southwest region of the Wake Island EEZ. In this video, check out a #carriercrab with a Dora-inspired backpack anemone. In addition to their long, thin walking legs, Homolidae crabs (also known as âporter crabsâ) have modified rear appendages they use to pick up #anemones and other things on the seafloor. Scientists speculate that this behavior could be related to physical camouflage, chemical camouflage, or predator defense.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value: We spotted this #bigfinsquid (genus #Magnapinna) with #ROVLittleHercules around 5,400 meters (17,716 feet) deep on the #abyssalplain in the waters of the Mariana Archipelago. Rarely seen on camera, this marine invertebrate is recognized by its distinct morphology, including perpendicular arms and tentacles that resemble elbows. Scientists understand the bigfin may be the deepest-dwelling of all #squid, as itâs been seen even below 6,000 meters in the hadal zone.

Rosencrantz & Guildenstern Are Dead is a 1990 black comedy adapted and directed by Tom Stoppard from his own 1966 play. The film follows two minor characters from Shakespeareâs Hamlet as they wander toward Elsinore, summoned to discover what ails the prince, while the tragedy of the Danish court unfolds around them almost as background noise. Gary Oldman plays Rosencrantz and Tim Roth plays Guildenstern, though the pair and everyone they meet keep mixing up their names. Richard Dreyfuss appears as the Player who leads a traveling troupe, with Iain Glen as Hamlet. Shot in and around Zagreb and Sloveniaâs BreÅ¾ice Castle, the movie opened at Venice in September 1990 and won the Golden Lion.

Stoppardâs screen version keeps the playâs verbal tennis, coin-flip experiments that always land heads, and debates about chance, identity, and whether anyone is actually in charge of their own story. Critics were divided on whether the material belonged on film rather than the stage, but most praised the two leads and Dreyfuss. The picture was only a modest box-office performer after its 1991 U.S. and U.K. releases, yet it remains a distinctive literary curiosity: a filmed play that treats Hamlet as a half-glimpsed catastrophe happening to people who never quite understand the script they are in.

ð§ ð Why is it that if two players leave the pool at the same time, they do not regain their body temperature at the same rate?

In short, metabolically more efficient individuals will rewarm faster.

Ref: Giacoppo et al. (2023) and SÃ¸berg, SchÃ©ele et al. (2021)

De kracht van wind! De wind is niet te zien, maar wel te voelen. Denk maar eens aan tegenwind op je fiets. Wat is wind eigenlijk? Wind is bewegende lucht in de atmosfeer, die ontstaat door verschillen in luchtdruk. Deze drukverschillen worden veroorzaakt door de ongelijkmatige opwarming van het aardoppervlak door de zon. JÃ¼rgen Klopp arrived at the Parc des Princes in late November 2018 with his Champions League campaign in trouble. A defeat to Red Star Belgrade earlier in the group had left Liverpool third in Group C, and a poor result against Paris Saint-Germain would put the previous season's finalists on the brink of an early exit. The pre-match press conference was held in Paris, which meant questions came in French and were relayed to Klopp through a translator speaking directly into his earpiece.

What happened next has outlived the match itself. After the first translated question, Klopp pulled the earpiece out, paused, and told the translator they had "a very erotic voice." He followed it with congratulations and a request to hear it again. Journalists in the room laughed for a long stretch, and Klopp sat there grinning through it. English and French coverage of the clip actually disagrees on whether the voice belonged to a man or a woman, which only added to the afterlife of the moment online.

The game the following night did not go Liverpool's way. PSG won 2-1 through Juan Bernat and Neymar, with James Milner converting a first-half penalty, and the Reds were left needing a specific result against Napoli at Anfield on the final matchday. They got it, edging through by a single goal, and the season ended with Klopp lifting the European Cup in Madrid after a 2-0 win over Tottenham. Seen from that distance, the press conference reads differently. A manager under real pressure chose to laugh out loud in public, and his squad went on to win the thing.

Brazil President Lula and Brazil election 2026.

Every foreign visit of the three Lula presidencies, flown in order across a Robinson world with shaded relief. 319 country-visits over 186 trips to 88 destinations, 1 January 2003 to 30 June 2026. A country darkens each time he returns to it, a bar tracks Brazil's own GDP year by year, and after 2010 he flies as hard as ever while the counter almost stops.

EVERYTHING THAT IS WRONG, UNCERTAIN OR APPROXIMATE IN THIS FILM, in one place.

Errors found in the source and corrected against the PresidÃªncia's own record:

1. Wikipedia gives the 2008 Rome visit as '19â13 November', an impossible range. The PresidÃªncia datelines him Roma â ItÃ¡lia on 11 November 2008 and puts him at Itamaraty on the 19th. Corrected to 11â13 November.

2. Wikipedia gives Helsinki as the city of the Norway leg of 13â14 September 2007. Helsinki is Finland's capital and is the city two rows above. The PresidÃªncia datelines the banquet with King Harald V as Oslo â Noruega, 13 September 2007. Corrected to Oslo.

3. Two legs are contradicted. The PresidÃªncia's record places Lula in Brazil on every claimed day of the Colombia visit of 27â28 June 2003 (BrasÃ­lia on the 27th, Parintins in Amazonas on the 28th) and of the Paraguay visit of 14â15 August 2003 (BrasÃ­lia both days, Foz do IguaÃ§u on the 16th), with no speech in either destination within three weeks. Both are still drawn, because removing a leg on my own judgement would be a bigger claim than leaving it in and saying so.

4. Forty-two legs the record is silent on, short working visits on days the speech archive holds nothing, 32 of them in 2007â2010. Silence is not a refutation.

5. Twelve legs' dates are off by a day, overlapping the neighbouring leg of the same tour.

Approximations I chose, and what they cost:

Little Britain is a British sketch comedy series created by and starring Matt Lucas and David Walliams that aired on BBC from 2003 to 2006.

The show is presented as a mockumentary narrated by Tom Baker, with the premise of showing the lives of bizarre, eccentric, and often outrageous characters from all corners of "Little Britain" - a satirical take on modern British life.

Instead of one storyline, it jumps between dozens of recurring characters, each with their own catchphrase and running gag:

*Some of the most iconic characters include:*
- *Lou and Andy* - Lou patiently looks after his friend Andy, who pretends to need a wheelchair
- *Vicky Pollard* - The fast-talking teenage gossip from Bristol - "Yeah but, no but, yeah but..."
- *Daffyd Thomas* - The self-proclaimed "only gay in the village" in Wales
- *Marjorie Dawes* - The leader of the FatFighters weight-loss group - "Dust?"
- *Emily Howard* - The unconvincing transvestite - "I'm a lady!"
- *Sebastian Love* - The Prime Minister's aide in love with the PM

Known for its over-the-top characters, absurd situations, and unforgettable catchphrases, the show became a huge cultural phenomenon in the UK, winning multiple BAFTA awards. It later spawned a US version, Little Britain USA, and live stage tours.

It's classic, surreal, and very British sketch comedy that defined an era of 2000s TV.

Paspocalypse (2024) is a Dutch horror short film directed by Jasper ten Hoor and Ivan Hidayat. The story follows Tina, a young cleaning woman working a late-night shift inside an empty office building. With the building deserted and only the sound of music playing through her earphones, Tina expects a quiet and uneventful night.

Her routine suddenly changes when she encounters a mannequin standing unexpectedly inside the building. Confused and unsettled, Tina moves the strange figure into a closet, hoping to put the disturbing encounter behind her. However, she soon realizes that the mannequin is not as harmless or stationary as it appears.

What follows is a tense cat-and-mouse chase through the deserted office complex, as Tina desperately tries to escape the mysterious threat. The film builds its horror through isolation, silence, and the unsettling uncertainty of whether what she is experiencing is real.

Starring Wendy Ruijfrok as Tina, Paspocalypse is a six-minute horror story that transforms an ordinary workplace into a terrifying environment.
